findings.title: Project uses motion but no prefers-reduced-motion policy was found
findings.description: A project-level reduced-motion policy is a more reliable safeguard than hoping each animated component handles the preference independently.
findings.suggestion: Add global reduced-motion CSS and make JavaScript animation systems consult matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').
findings.bad: animations throughout the project, no reduced-motion branch
findings.snippet: Motion detected; no prefers-reduced-motion policy found.

findings.title: Effect may update a dependency it watches
findings.description: An effect that writes to a value represented in its own dependency list can become a render loop or repeated side-effect cascade.
findings.suggestion: Derive values directly where possible, or ensure the update converges and depends on a distinct source value.
findings.good: const nextCount = count + 1; // derive, or update only from an external event

findings.title: Unstable React key generated during render
findings.description: Keys must describe stable identity. Generating a new key remounts components, loses local state and creates unnecessary DOM work.
findings.suggestion: Use a durable entity ID. If the source lacks one, create identity when data enters the system rather than during rendering.

findings.title: Many unrelated high z-index values
findings.description: Several unrelated high stacking values indicate local escalation rather than a controlled layer system.
findings.suggestion: Replace numeric competition with named layer tokens and document which component types own each layer.

findings.title: Possible state array mutation
findings.description: Mutating an existing state array preserves its reference and can produce missed renders or hard-to-track shared mutations.
findings.suggestion: Create a new array when updating state.

findings.title: Image missing alt attribute
findings.description: Images without alt text lack an accessible text alternative. Decorative images should explicitly use an empty alt.
findings.suggestion: Add concise meaningful alt text, or alt="" for decorative imagery.

findings.title: Clickable div without native button semantics
findings.description: A div with click behavior is not keyboard-operable or announced as a control by default.
findings.suggestion: Use a button for actions and an anchor for navigation. Native elements provide keyboard and accessibility behavior automatically.

findings.title: Arbitrary high z-index
findings.description: Large local z-index values create stacking-context escalation and modal or tooltip conflicts.
findings.suggestion: Define a short layer scale such as base, sticky, dropdown, overlay, modal and toast.

findings.title: Very small interactive padding
findings.description: Tiny target padding increases missed taps and can make adjacent destructive actions dangerous on touch screens.
findings.suggestion: Aim for a comfortable touch target around 44 by 44 CSS pixels where practical.

findings.title: Motion exists without reduced-motion handling in this file
findings.description: Users who request reduced motion should not receive the same non-essential animation by default.
findings.suggestion: Add a reduced-motion media query or framework equivalent. A project-level policy may satisfy this even if it lives elsewhere.
findings.snippet: .card { animation: breathe 2s ease-in-out infinite; transition: width 500ms, box-shadow 500ms; }

findings.title: Focus outline removed
findings.description: Removing the focus indicator can make keyboard navigation impossible to track unless an equally visible replacement exists.
findings.suggestion: Provide a visible :focus-visible treatment before removing the browser outline.

findings.title: Large fixed width
findings.description: Large fixed widths frequently overflow narrow screens and fail under text zoom.
findings.suggestion: Use max-width plus fluid width, and test around 320 to 400 CSS pixels.

findings.title: Production console.log candidate
findings.description: Debug logging left in application code can leak information, add noise and hide meaningful diagnostics.
findings.suggestion: Remove it or route structured diagnostics through an environment-aware logger.

findings.title: 100vw horizontal overflow risk
findings.description: 100vw can include scrollbar width and produce a small horizontal bleed on desktop or nested layouts.
findings.suggestion: Prefer width: 100% for normal page flow. Use viewport width only when the viewport itself is the intended reference.

findings.title: Forced viewport-height section
findings.description: Repeated viewport-height sections can create artificial gaps and mobile browser viewport issues.
findings.suggestion: Use content-driven height unless the viewport is a real interaction requirement. Consider dynamic viewport units where appropriate.

findings.title: Image missing explicit dimensions
findings.description: Images without intrinsic dimensions can create layout shift while the browser discovers their aspect ratio.
findings.suggestion: Provide width and height attributes or a CSS aspect-ratio with reserved layout space.

findings.title: Email input missing autocomplete
findings.description: Autocomplete metadata improves form completion, password-manager interoperability and mobile keyboard behavior.
findings.suggestion: Use autocomplete="email" for account email fields unless there is a specific reason not to.

findings.title: Form input missing name
findings.description: Unnamed controls are omitted from native form submission and are harder for tooling to understand.
findings.suggestion: Give form controls stable semantic names unless they are intentionally non-submitting UI controls.

findings.title: Password input missing autocomplete
findings.description: Correct password autocomplete values help password managers distinguish sign-in from password creation.
findings.suggestion: Use current-password for sign-in and new-password for account creation or reset flows.

findings.title: Glassmorphism surface
findings.description: Blurred translucent panels can reduce contrast, add GPU cost and flatten hierarchy when used everywhere.
findings.suggestion: Reserve blur for a specific layering need. Prefer opaque surfaces for primary reading regions.

findings.title: Multiple animation libraries detected
findings.description: Multiple animation systems increase bundle size, mental overhead and inconsistent motion behavior.
findings.suggestion: Standardize on the smallest set that covers actual product requirements.
findings.good: one primary motion system plus native CSS transitions where sufficient

findings.title: Infinite animation
findings.description: Continuous decorative motion consumes attention and resources long after it has communicated anything useful.
findings.suggestion: Use finite motion for state transitions. If continuous animation is meaningful, respect reduced-motion and provide pause behavior when appropriate.
findings.snippet: .card { animation: breathe 2s ease-in-out infinite; transition: width 500ms, box-shadow 500ms; }

findings.title: Potentially expensive animated property
findings.description: Animating layout or heavy paint properties can produce avoidable frame drops on lower-end devices.
findings.suggestion: Prefer transform and opacity for high-frequency visual motion when the visual result is equivalent.
findings.snippet: .card { animation: breathe 2s ease-in-out infinite; transition: width 500ms, box-shadow 500ms; }

findings.title: Potentially expensive animated property

findings.suggestion: Prefer transform and opacity for high-frequency visual motion when the visual result is equivalent.
findings.snippet: @keyframes breathe { from { filter: blur(0); } to { filter: blur(4px); } }

findings.title: Purple-to-blue gradient fingerprint
findings.description: A familiar purple-to-blue gradient often appears as default template personality rather than a product-specific color decision.
findings.suggestion: Keep it only when it is part of an intentional brand system. Prefer named design tokens and a restrained accent strategy.

findings.title: Gradient-clipped text
findings.description: Gradient text is frequently used to manufacture hierarchy instead of earning it through typography and copy.
findings.suggestion: Verify the heading remains distinctive with a normal foreground color. Use scale, weight and measure first.
findings.good: Build software your team can operate.

findings.title: Image without lazy-loading hint
findings.description: Non-critical images can compete with essential resources when loaded eagerly. Hero images may correctly remain eager.
findings.suggestion: Use loading="lazy" for below-the-fold content. Keep important LCP imagery eager and prioritized deliberately.

findings.title: Arbitrary border radius
findings.description: One-off radii are a common signal of a design system drifting into local guesses.
findings.suggestion: Use a small documented radius scale and assign radii by component role.

findings.title: Multiple icon libraries detected
findings.description: Multiple icon sets can create inconsistent stroke language and ship duplicate glyph infrastructure.
findings.suggestion: Choose a primary icon family and allow exceptions only when a specific symbol is unavailable.

findings.title: Inter used as global identity
findings.description: Inter is excellent, but using it by default can make unrelated products converge visually.
findings.suggestion: Keep Inter when it suits the product. Otherwise define a deliberate type system with fallback metrics and clear hierarchy.
